findings.title: Substring match treats negated or OR'd event.type:error filters as error-only
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the raw query string contains the substring `event.type:error`. That also matches `!event.type:error` (selects non-error rows such as transactions) and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. For such queries on the discover dataset with all projects allowlisted, `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()` = `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. Transaction rows carry no sample_weight, so the result is zero or wrong counts presented as upsampled error counts, with no error raised. The unit test only covers a positive case and an unrelated query, so this is not caught. The check should parse the query and look for a standalone, non-negated `event.type:error` term.

findings.title: upsampled_count is exposed as a general-purpose aggregate with no guard
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered in the global discover function converter, so any user can type `upsampled_count()` in any discover/events query on any dataset. There is no allowlist or dataset check. The aggregate is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, which is null or zero for events without sample_weight (non-allowlisted projects, transactions). Users therefore get silently low numbers, or a query error on datasets lacking the column. The comment 'assumes sample_weight exists' is not enforced anywhere, and the function has no unit test.

findings.title: 'upsampled_count() as count' is an alias form the other column paths don't use
findings.body: The transformed column string `upsampled_count() as count` is passed directly as a selected/y-axis column to `timeseries_query` and `top_events_timeseries`. Every other aggregate in these paths is a bare `func(args)` string, and this change adds no parsing for an ` as alias` suffix. If the field parser rejects this string, every upsampled request fails with an invalid-field error instead of returning counts, and the endpoint test expecting `count == 10` would fail. This needs verification against the parser. Either confirm the alias form is supported or use the bare function and map the result key separately.

findings.title: Only an exact count() is upsampled, so mixed column lists produce inconsistent values
findings.body: The transform rewrites a column only when it equals `count()` after lowercasing and stripping. Equations that reference count (for example `equation|count() / 2`) are passed through unchanged. A single chart can therefore show an upsampled `count` series next to an equation computed from the raw, un-upsampled count. Nothing in the code or tests handles this mixed case, and the function silently leaves those columns alone.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is re-evaluated on every _get_event_stats call, even for non-count queries
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` runs unconditionally at the start of every `_get_event_stats` call. For dashboard widgets this happens up to four times per request, each doing a cache read and possibly a cache write plus an options lookup. It runs even when no requested column is `count()`, which is the only thing the transform affects. The check should be skipped unless a count column is present.

findings.title: Allowlist lookup and cache write happen before the cheap dataset check
findings.body: `is_eligible` (an options read plus a cache write on a miss) is computed before `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, which is a simple dataset comparison. For transactions, spans, or metrics queries, which never upsample, every call still reads options and writes the cache. The final result is `is_eligible and ...` with the cheap check second. The dataset/query check should run first and short-circuit.

findings.title: Allowlist changes take up to 60s to apply and the invalidation helper is never called
findings.body: The eligibility result is cached for 60 seconds (`cache.set` at line 38), keyed only on organization and project set. Allowlist edits therefore take up to a minute to affect counts. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined to be called 'when the allowlist configuration changes', but nothing in the diff calls it, so it is dead code and the consistency it promises does not exist. Either wire it into the option-change path or remove it and document the staleness window.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses the outer dataset, not the dataset actually queried
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` receives the outer `dataset`, but `_get_event_stats` runs against `scoped_dataset`, and the widget split path passes a different `split_dataset` (for example `discover` with `event.type:transaction`). The decision therefore describes a different dataset from the one queried. The split path currently only runs when the outer dataset is a metrics dataset, so this is latent. If that gating changes, a transactions-only split query would be upsampled whenever the outer dataset is errors. The dataset actually being queried should be passed.

findings.title: Comments claim caching and performance guarantees the code does not provide
findings.body: The comments describe an 'early upsampling eligibility check for performance optimization' whose 'cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution', and say storing the decision 'allows for better query optimization and caching'. None of this holds. `should_upsample` is a local boolean, nothing is cached at this level, and the check is re-run on every `_get_event_stats` call. The 'late transformation ensures we use the most current schema assumptions' comment is also unsupported. These should be corrected so maintainers don't assume a caching guarantee that doesn't exist.

findings.title: Unrelated change to a public error message
findings.body: The `topEvents` validation message changes from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is unrelated to upsampling and changes the `detail` string returned by the public API. Any client or existing test matching the old text will break. The fix should be split into its own change, or confirmed safe with a check of existing tests and consumers.

findings.title: Stray submodule-pointer file committed at repository root
findings.body: The PR adds a regular file named `sentry-repo` whose content is `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`. This is not a real submodule: no `.gitmodules` entry or gitlink is added, so git treats it as an ordinary text file. It pollutes the repository root with a pointer to the base commit, and it can confuse checkout or any later real submodule setup under that name. It is almost certainly an accidental commit and should be removed.

findings.title: Bare exception swallowing in test helper that runs for every store_event
findings.body: Both `try/except Exception: pass` blocks in `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` silently discard any error, including a malformed `contexts` value or an unparsable rate. A malformed test event then just loses its sample_rate, and the test depending on it fails far from the cause, or passes incorrectly. Because the helper is called from `store_event` for the whole test suite, this hides problems globally. The handling should be narrowed to the expected cases, or errors should be allowed to surface.

findings.title: Modified topEvents, RPC, and widget-split paths have no test coverage
findings.body: The new test class only exercises the plain timeseries path with `count()`. The `topEvents` branch (where `top_events_timeseries` now receives transformed columns), the RPC branches, and the dashboard widget split path in `get_event_stats_factory` are all modified by this PR but have no tests. There are also no tests for negated or OR'd `event.type` queries, which is why the substring bug in error_upsampling.py went unnoticed, and no direct tests for the `upsampled_count` aggregate or the cache behavior. Coverage should be added for `topEvents=` and a widget-split case, plus the negation case.
